subject: Post-demo: data handling requirements & DPA clarifications for MedCura
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@medcura.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@medcura.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: data handling requirements & DPA clarifications for MedCura

Hi Liam / Priya,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation and helpful signals on the production constraints. Quick recap and asks so we can get legal/security aligned on your side:

1) Data residency: you called out a requirement to keep PHI/PII within us-east-2. Can you confirm whether that needs to apply to all inference and logs, or only persisted storage?

2) Retention: you mentioned retention of patient records for 7+ years for auditability. On Redwood's side we typically offer configurable retention windows; default audit logs are 90 days. Would MedCura require an explicit contractual retention commit?

3) Logging & evidence: you asked for exportable access logs and per-request metadata (request ID, model, timestamp). We can provide structured logs and a downloadable export. Any specific schema or fields you need?

4) Controller/Processor: legal flagged a few DPA lines around responsibilities and subprocessors — specifically notice timelines for subprocessor changes and incident notification timelines.

I've attached our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and a SOC2 stub for initial evidence. Can you confirm which of the above are hard blockers vs. nice-to-haves?

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm residency scope and retention policy (MedCura)
- We will surface subprocessor list and incident notification playbook (Redwood)
- If helpful, we can have a short triage call with Security (30m) to go through technical controls.

If this looks right, I'll kick off the redline and route to legal.

Thanks,

Grace O'Connor
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@medcura.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@medcura.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 18:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling requirements & DPA clarifications for MedCura

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the clear recap. Prioritization from our side:
- Residency: hard blocker — all persisted data (model inputs/outputs and logs) must reside in us-east-2.
- Retention: we need a contractual maximum retention cap for patient-linked data of 7 years; logs can be shorter if they are pseudonymized but we need a chain of custody.
- Incident notification: legal prefers notification "without undue delay" and to see a timeline (we usually ask partners to agree to 24–72 hours for confirmed breaches).
- Subprocessors: we require a 30-day advance notice for any new subprocessor that would access PHI.

Questions for you:
1) Does Redwood offer per-client isolated storage within a region (single-tenant data buckets) or is it tenant-separated logical controls?
2) For deletion on contract termination, what is the guaranteed purge window and proof of deletion?

Also looping Priya (security) — Priya, can you add any missing items?

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

-Liam
Liam O'Neill

Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling requirements & DPA clarifications for MedCura

Hi Liam / Grace,

Quick technical clarifications (happy to expand on a call):

1) Residency & storage: Redwood supports region-scoped tenant data placements. For customers requiring stronger isolation, we offer per-customer dedicated S3 buckets and VPC endpoints in the chosen region (us-east-2) under our Dedicated/Private options. Hosted tenants are logically separated; for strict PHI/BAA workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.

2) Retention & deletion: We support configurable retention policies per dataset. For deletion after termination we offer a contractual deletion window (default 30 days) and can provide signed deletion certificates + a deletion job run log. If you require a shorter window or formal proof-of-destruction, we can capture a hash-based proof for archived copies.

3) Logs & schema: We emit structured JSON logs that include request_id, model_id, timestamp, client_tenant_id, and event_type. We can include additional custom fields (e.g., patient_id pseudonym) but recommend pseudonymization before sending PHI into the system. Exportable logs are available via our S3 export job.

4) Subprocessors & notice: Our current subprocessors list is available (see link). For PHI access, we require subprocessors to be under contractual obligations equivalent to our DPA. Standard policy is to notify customers in advance; 30-day notice is reasonable. For emergency patching that requires short-term access we'd request an exception process with immediate notice.

5) Incident notification: Our playbook distinguishes:
- T0: detection & containment (internal)
- T+24h: preliminary notification to impacted customers if a confirmed user-impacting event is suspected
- T+72h: detailed incident notification once scope is known
We can include a clause for an initial notification within 24–48 hours and a fuller report by 72 hours depending on investigations.

Happy to schedule a 30-minute security triage with Priya to walk through the controls and evidence pack.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Staff Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling requirements & DPA clarifications for MedCura

Thanks Dev — that helps. A couple follow-ups before we loop legal:

- Deletion window: default 30 days is acceptable but we need an option to accelerate to 7 days for specific datasets (contractually enforceable). Can Redwood commit to that on contract?
- Subprocessors: 30-day notice is okay, but MedCura requires an explicit opt-out clause for subprocessors that will process PHI (we would prefer to approve/not-approve). Is that something Redwood will entertain for enterprise accounts?
- Incident timeline: we will take the 24–72h framework to legal, but please confirm that the 24h preliminary notification is for confirmed incidents only (not false positives).

If we can get these answers in writing, I can push a redline to legal this week.

-Priya (copied) — please add anything on the technical evidence you'd like to see (encryption keys, key management, signing certs).

Regards,
Liam

Liam / Priya — thanks for the clarifying Qs. Proposed next steps so we can keep momentum:

1) Redwood will produce a short redline to the attached DPA that:
   - exposes an accelerated deletion SLA option (7-day purge) as an addendum for specific datasets
   - clarifies region-scoped dedicated storage options (us-east-2) and the accessible evidence types
   - includes the 30-day subprocessor notice; we will surface an enterprise opt-out process for PHI-accessing subprocessors for customers on Dedicated/Private plans (legal will propose language).

2) We'll confirm incident notification language: preliminary notification for confirmed incidents within 24–48 hours, full report by 72 hours. We will avoid sending noise for false positives.

3) I'll attach a DocuSign packet for the DPA and a short evidence pack (SOC2 stub, KMS overview). Please expect a redline return by EOD Monday.
